events.title: Adolf Hitler Appointed Chancellor of Germany
events.description: President Paul von Hindenburg appointed Adolf Hitler as Chancellor of Germany, leading a coalition government between the Nazi Party and the conservative German National People's Party.
events.significance: Marked the start of the Nazi regime, which rapidly dismantled German democracy and led to World War II and the Holocaust.

events.title: Assassination of Mahatma Gandhi
events.description: Mohandas Karamchand Gandhi was shot and killed by Nathuram Godse while walking to a prayer meeting at Birla House in New Delhi, five months after India gained independence.
events.significance: The death of the leader of India's nonviolent independence movement shocked the world and prompted national mourning; January 30 is observed in India as Martyrs' Day.

events.title: Execution of King Charles I of England
events.description: Charles I was beheaded outside the Banqueting House in Whitehall, London, after being convicted of high treason by a High Court of Justice during the aftermath of the English Civil War.
events.significance: The only public execution of an English monarch, it led to the abolition of the monarchy and the establishment of the Commonwealth under Oliver Cromwell.

events.title: Start of the Tet Offensive
events.description: North Vietnamese and Viet Cong forces launched coordinated surprise attacks on cities and military bases across South Vietnam during the Tet lunar new year holiday.
events.significance: Though a military defeat for the communists, the offensive shattered American public confidence in the war's progress and became a turning point in US opinion and policy on Vietnam.

events.title: Birth of Franklin D. Roosevelt
events.description: Franklin Delano Roosevelt, the future 32nd President of the United States, was born in Hyde Park, New York.
events.significance: Roosevelt led the US through the Great Depression and most of World War II, and his New Deal programs reshaped the role of the federal government.
